tier1.text: Each lung lets the blood pick up oxygen and give off carbon dioxide, which we then breathe out. Each lung holds about 300 million alveoli, tiny grape-like sacs where the gases are swapped. The right lung is larger and has three lobes, or sections, while the smaller left lung has two.

tier2.text: The main job of each lung is gas exchange: swapping oxygen and carbon dioxide with the outside air. The lungs lie in the chest cavity, which also holds the heart in the mediastinum, the space between the lungs. The right lung has three lobes, the smaller units a lung is made of, and is shorter, wider and larger than the left lung. The left lung, in contrast, is longer and narrower, with two lobes and a dent called the cardiac notch that makes room for the tip of the heart. Each lung is attached only at the hilum, a point on the lung's inner side where the bronchi, the tubes that carry air in and out, enter with blood vessels and nerves. The bronchi branch into smaller and smaller passages that end in alveoli, tiny grape-like sacs in the lung where gas exchange takes place. Oxygen passes from the alveoli into the blood, while carbon dioxide, a waste product of the body's cells, passes from the blood into the alveoli to be breathed out. Each lung is enclosed in the pleura, a two-layered membrane: one layer is firmly attached to the lung, and the other lines the chest wall. The lungs do not move by themselves: sticky pleural fluid between the two layers makes the lungs follow the chest wall outward when we breathe in. Normal breathing out takes no energy, because the elastic lung tissue springs back as the breathing muscles relax.

sentences.text: The main job of each lung is gas exchange: swapping oxygen and carbon dioxide with the outside air.

quotes.quote: The main function of the lungs is to perform the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide with air from the atmosphere.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: Gas exchange occurs at two sites in the body: in the lungs, where oxygen is picked up and carbon dioxide is released at the respiratory membrane, and at the tissues, where oxygen is released and carbon dioxide is picked up.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The lungs lie in the chest cavity, which also holds the heart in the mediastinum, the space between the lungs.

quotes.quote: The thoracic cavity contains the lungs and the heart, which is located in the mediastinum.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: The human heart is located within the thoracic cavity, medially between the lungs in the space known as the mediastinum.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The right lung has three lobes, the smaller units a lung is made of, and is shorter, wider and larger than the left lung.

quotes.quote: The right lung is shorter, broader, and has a greater volume than the left lung. It is divided into three lobes and each lobe is supplied by one of the secondary bronchi.
quotes.section: SEER Training Modules: Bronchi, Bronchial Tree, & Lungs
quotes.citation: SEER Training Modules: Bronchi, Bronchial Tree, & Lungs. U.S. National Institutes of Health, National Cancer Institute.

sentences.text: The left lung, in contrast, is longer and narrower, with two lobes and a dent called the cardiac notch that makes room for the tip of the heart.

quotes.quote: The left lung is longer and narrower than the right lung. It has an indentation, called the cardiac notch, on its medial surface for the apex of the heart. The left lung has two lobes.
quotes.section: SEER Training Modules: Bronchi, Bronchial Tree, & Lungs
quotes.citation: SEER Training Modules: Bronchi, Bronchial Tree, & Lungs. U.S. National Institutes of Health, National Cancer Institute.

sentences.text: Each lung is attached only at the hilum, a point on the lung's inner side where the bronchi, the tubes that carry air in and out, enter with blood vessels and nerves.

quotes.quote: The only point of attachment for each lung is at the hilum, or root, on the medial side. This is where the bronchi, blood vessels, lymphatics, and nerves enter the lungs.
quotes.section: SEER Training Modules: Bronchi, Bronchial Tree, & Lungs
quotes.citation: SEER Training Modules: Bronchi, Bronchial Tree, & Lungs. U.S. National Institutes of Health, National Cancer Institute.

quotes.quote: bronchus: tube connected to the trachea that branches into many subsidiaries and provides a passageway for air to enter and leave the lungs
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The bronchi branch into smaller and smaller passages that end in alveoli, tiny grape-like sacs in the lung where gas exchange takes place.

quotes.quote: The bronchi branch into smaller and smaller passageways until they terminate in tiny air sacs called alveoli.
quotes.section: SEER Training Modules: Bronchi, Bronchial Tree, & Lungs
quotes.citation: SEER Training Modules: Bronchi, Bronchial Tree, & Lungs. U.S. National Institutes of Health, National Cancer Institute.

quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Oxygen passes from the alveoli into the blood, while carbon dioxide, a waste product of the body's cells, passes from the blood into the alveoli to be breathed out.

quotes.quote: Such intimate contact ensures that oxygen will diffuse from alveoli into the blood and be distributed to the cells of the body. In addition, the carbon dioxide that was produced by cells as a waste product will diffuse from the blood into alveoli to be exhaled.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Each lung is enclosed in the pleura, a two-layered membrane: one layer is firmly attached to the lung, and the other lines the chest wall.

quotes.quote: Each lung is enclosed by a double-layered serous membrane, called the pleura. The visceral pleura is firmly attached to the surface of the lung. At the hilum, the visceral pleura is continuous with the parietal pleura that lines the wall of the thorax.
quotes.section: SEER Training Modules: Bronchi, Bronchial Tree, & Lungs
quotes.citation: SEER Training Modules: Bronchi, Bronchial Tree, & Lungs. U.S. National Institutes of Health, National Cancer Institute.

sentences.text: The lungs do not move by themselves: sticky pleural fluid between the two layers makes the lungs follow the chest wall outward when we breathe in.

quotes.quote: The lungs themselves are passive during breathing, meaning they are not involved in creating the movement that helps inspiration and expiration. This is because of the adhesive nature of the pleural fluid, which allows the lungs to be pulled outward when the thoracic wall moves during inspiration.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: pleural fluid: substance that acts as a lubricant for the visceral and parietal layers of the pleura during the movement of breathing
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Normal breathing out takes no energy, because the elastic lung tissue springs back as the breathing muscles relax.

quotes.quote: The process of normal expiration is passive, meaning that energy is not required to push air out of the lungs. Instead, the elasticity of the lung tissue causes the lung to recoil, as the diaphragm and intercostal muscles relax following inspiration.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
